publicBrief.acceptedPolicy: Creating a note requires the POST global note/document permissions and an owner-aware change_document check on the target document; viewing the document alone is insufficient.
publicBrief.currentQuestion: At DocumentViewSet.notes POST handler entry, can an authenticated user who has all listed global POST permissions and an object view grant on a document create a note when a different user owns the document and the caller has no object change_document grant?
premises: At notes POST entry, the authenticated caller has the global POST permissions and an object view grant, but is not the document owner and lacks its object change_document grant.
requiredResponseDetails: Separate the global PaperlessNotePermissions check, the object view check, the object change check, and Note.objects.create effect.

results.explanation: At the declared notes POST entry, the handler binds the caller from request.user and loads the target Document by pk with its owner (src-326d35bf1de38682:1848-1855). The action declares PaperlessNotePermissions, which is the visible global permission gate at entry, but the supplied crop does not include that class's implementation; the task premise supplies that the global POST permissions pass. The separate object view check calls has_perms_owner_aware for view_document and returns HTTP 403 before method dispatch when it fails (src-326d35bf1de38682:1857-1862); under the premise, the object-view check passes. In the POST branch, a separate owner-aware change_document check is performed and returns HTTP 403 when it fails (src-326d35bf1de38682:1877-1886). The supplied owner-aware helper permits an object when it has no owner, the caller is the owner, or the object-permission checker grants the requested permission (src-9568837fbfe275f5:624-635). Given the stated different-owner and no-object-change premises, that decisive check fails. Therefore Note.objects.create is not reached; the protected note-creation effect is the call shown at src-326d35bf1de38682:1888-1892, which would bind the note to the loaded document, request data, and caller. The source-visible result is deny. No decisive source-external fact is needed for this declared-entry assessment; deployment behavior and the implementation details of PaperlessNotePermissions are not needed because the task premise states the global gate passes and the object change check independently blocks the effect.

citations.quote:
def has_perms_owner_aware(user, perms, obj):
    """
    Legacy slow path (guardian-backed) single-object permission check.

    The queryset-filtering side of this migrated onto
    ``PermittedObjectsFilter``/``permitted_object_ids()``, but this
    single-object check still has many production callers. Several callers
    remain across ``documents/``, ``paperless_mail/``, and ``paperless_ai/``
    -- grep for this function name before removing it.
    """
    checker = ObjectPermissionChecker(user)
    return obj.owner is None or obj.owner == user or checker.has_perm(perms, obj)
